title: Compile the width-13 Clifford decoder into 4,265 Bell reads and certify its dense input cost (no κ)
body:
## Result

This takes the implementation-cost handoff from #7799. The width-13 Clifford decoder compiles into **4,265 distinct signed Bell-block reads per symplectic fibre**, shared by its 256 Pauli coefficients. For the identity coefficient, on arbitrary dense computational-basis observations, the exact number of required scalar reads is **151 × 2⁴⁷ = 21,251,360,741,654,528**. [Compiler and examples](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fdc90699f4a64139ed6d84cdbf9a606ff0ccd32e/research/clifford-sparse-row/README.md) · [Group certificate](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fdc90699f4a64139ed6d84cdbf9a606ff0ccd32e/research/clifford-sparse-row/PROOF.md) · [Raw acquisition and tape costs](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fdc90699f4a64139ed6d84cdbf9a606ff0ccd32e/research/clifford-sparse-row/COST.md)

Grouping the shear characters by their actual three-plane and quotienting repeated cosets reduces the source's double character sum. Direct expansion checks all 34,120 signed terms on 8,304 distinct symplectic elements. Only the target survives. The package emits the block addresses, exact weights and transport phases. An independent 64-operator mixture test recovers 512 coefficients for two fibres.

The identity traces share 22 shift geometries. Their frequencies use at most ten independent binary directions per geometry. Exhausting all 10,530 parity assignments proves that the combined raw coefficients have two nonzero magnitudes, 1/32 and 1/8. The executable supports random lookup and an address generator which enumerates each required input exactly once. The dense-input lower bound follows by perturbing one unread coordinate. Each normalized coefficient row has squared Euclidean norm 2⁴⁵. For the whole decoder we obtain an operator norm at most 4¹²√(1319/64), below 2²⁷.

These bounds apply to the emitted realization. Coalescing equivalent coset observations preserves recovery on the Clifford-mixture image and specifies an extension on arbitrary noise. Other decoder rows and compact or pretransformed inputs can have different access costs. The record-tape result counts input-head moves separately from arithmetic and workspace movement. No physical supplier or improvement to κ is claimed.

## Verification

All eight registered runs passed on CPython 3.12.14. They include normal and optimized runs of the compiler, raw address checks, independent literal tensor checks and mixture recovery. Standard library only.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-sparse-row
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/clifford-sparse-row --check-source-history --check-modes
python3.12 -B research/clifford-sparse-row/raw_row.py --probe-index 0
```

The raw verifier checks 21,060 cell-boundary lookups, the exact row norm, the extreme addresses and normalized diagonal Clifford column recovery. Separate literal tests check 262,144 shear phases, 24,576 transvection columns and six sparse raw inputs covering both signs, both magnitudes and cancellation. The enormous dense input is counted algebraically. It is never materialized.

Committed bytes, modes, source history and the official export passed. All eight checks also passed from a read-only Git-free export with an empty PATH. Local verification is independent of hosted workflow status.
